summary: Thomas R. Trautmann is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was attested in 1991 as a professor of history and anthropology at the University of Michigan.
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy from around 1782 to 1784, at Jesus College, Cambridge in 1784, and at the University of Cambridge from circa 1784 to 1788.

Thomas Roebuck was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He became assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811 and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1811–1819).
Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his B.A. studying at Queen's University Belfast (1857–1861) and Queen's University of Ireland (~1857–1861).
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Buddhist studies scholar Thubten Chodron studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery under several teachers, including Lama Thubten Yeshe. She served at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation before founding Sravasti Abbey in 2003.

Thubten Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Agvan Dorzhiev. He held a post attested in 1988 at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center and taught Jeffrey Hopkins, Steven Neal Weinberger, Amy Sims Miller, and Chogye Trichen.

Thubten Jigme Norbu studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Geshe Ngawang Nyima in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and was a professor at Indiana University from 1965 to 1992.
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Tenzin Gyatso, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche studied under teachers including Lama Thubten Yeshe and Tenzin Gyatso. He founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, the Lama Yeshe Wisdom Archive, and Maitripa College, and became spiritual director of the Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition in 1984.

Thupten Jinpa studied at Zongkar Choede, Ganden Monastery, and Cambridge. He founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics, served as its chief editor (~1996), was a research fellow at Girton College (1996–1999), and was a visiting research scholar at Stanford.

Thupten Samphel was a Tibetology scholar who studied at St. Stephen's College (~1974–1977), the University of Delhi (~1974–1979), and Columbia University (~1981–1982). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1845. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Thích Minh Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (~1957–1961). He lectured in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1953–1961) and served as Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (~1964–1975).
Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and completed his doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University by 1977.

Tianshu Zhu studied at Northwest University (MA) and Ohio State University (PhD) under John C. Huntington. She held posts at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Korea University, and Ohio State University, working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies.

Tiberius Hemsterhuis studied at Leiden University (~1701–1704) in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1704–1717), the University of Franeker (~1717–1740), and Leiden University (1740–1765).

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, earning his PhD. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he was a professor at Leiden University from circa 1976 to 2002.

Timothy H. Barrett studied at the University of Cambridge and Yale University. A scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.
